clue.text: Speaking budgie, oddly, gets hostile attention?

indicators.note: speaking says the picked letters are to be said out loud as a phrase
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word budgie

explanation.surface: A talking pet bird, behaving strangely, draws a glare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks B, D, I from budgie; said as letter names they sound like 'bee dee eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspicious, watchful gaze is the stock idiom for keeping a wary, unfriendly eye on someone.

clue.text: Very close hybrid of rodent and ox

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross-bred mixture, so the letters of the two animals are mixed together

explanation.surface: A creature bred from a rat and a bullock is nearly the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something said to be in the adjacent house is figuratively very near or nearly the same.

clue.text: Animals with long faces sleep upside down

indicators.note: in a down light, upside down means the joined words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: people with long faces look sad
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Glum-looking creatures doze hanging inverted, like bats.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the giant and red species are both well-known mammals, so a general word for creatures covers them.

clue.text: Attack row of cages

definitions.meaning: a set of cages for hens in intensive egg farming

explanation.surface: Assault on a line of coops.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term for unlawful physical violence, and the farming term for tiers of hen cages.

clue.text: One coaxing Turner to capture daughter

indicators.note: to capture means the first word surrounds the second, holding it inside

parts.note: a wheeler is something that wheels or turns

explanation.surface: A sweet-talker persuades the painter Turner to kidnap his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J M W Turner; it is just something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who uses flattery and coaxing to persuade someone is a cajoler.

clue.text: Change of tone, when fifty overwhelmed by disease

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the first word is engulfed by the illness word around it

parts.note: an infection is a disease
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone's voice alters when an epidemic swamps fifty people.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a modulation in the pitch of the voice when speaking.

clue.text: Seal discussed, little one owned by the Crown, perhaps?

definitions.text: little one owned by the Crown, perhaps?

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so the seal word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a signet ring

explanation.surface: A seal is talked over: a tiny thing that might belong to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: By tradition the British monarch owns unmarked mute swans on open water, hence the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a young swan is a little one, and swans are traditionally royal property in Britain.

clue.text: Sweet thing, a magnificent sea reflection?

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the joined words appear backwards

parts.note: rare can mean excellent or magnificent, as in a rare treat
MED is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A sweet seen as a gorgeous sea's mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a coarse brown sugar from Guyana, so a sweetener.

clue.text: Fine muscular swimmer

parts.note: hunky means muscular and attractive
a dory is a fish, so a swimmer

explanation.surface: A well-built swimmer in fine shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a person; here it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: everything being satisfactory or all right.

clue.text: Stretch of road I took, underground passage

indicators.note: Stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller recalls a route that led through a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mining term: a near-horizontal entrance tunnel into a mine.

clue.text: Act entitled to be amended — where to ratify it?

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the letters of entitled are rearranged

explanation.surface: A titled Act of Parliament is to be amended: where should it be signed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act entitled' reads as a legal bill; Act is just a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: you sign on the broken printed line at the foot of a document to make it binding.

clue.text: See 18
Fabric he altered with large cut for religious leader

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of these two words are rearranged
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: big means large

explanation.surface: A cloth refashioned with a big chunk cut out, for a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: the chief religious authority of a Jewish community, e.g. in Britain.

clue.text: Business heading west in report, move premises

indicators.note: in places the reversed business word inside the report word

parts.note: to relate is to report or tell

indicators.note: heading west means read right to left in an across answer

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A firm going west, according to a report, changes its address.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to set up in a new place, as a firm moving its offices.

clue.text: Driven thing with little power, sadly Blair not in control

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters sit inside the control word

parts.note: a rein controls a horse; to rein in is to control

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, sadly not in charge, is left with little power.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a three-wheeled British car of the 1970s to 2000s, famously underpowered.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small British three-wheeler car with a modest engine, so a weakly powered vehicle.

clue.text: Producing a score, composer at first in love

indicators.note: in puts the first letter inside the love word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so nothing

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of composer

explanation.surface: A composer, first in love, writes music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' suggests music; here it is cutting tallies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: to notch is to score, as in making nicks or tallying points.

clue.text: Troll, rather ugly, immediately starts texting platitudes

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

parts.note: SMS is the text message service

explanation.surface: An ugly online troll starts sending messages full of clichés.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: self-evident statements that are too obvious to be worth saying.

clue.text: Make up scene with demons dancing around marshland

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the marshland word
dancing means the letters jig about into a new order

parts.note: a fen is marshland, as in the Fens of East Anglia

explanation.surface: A spooky scene of demons dancing over a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to restore good relations after a quarrel, as friends do when they reconcile.

clue.text: Calm down, feeding vegetables to animal

indicators.note: feeding means putting the vegetables into the animal

parts.note: an ape is an animal
peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: Settle down while giving greens to a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to pacify or soothe someone who is angry.

clue.text: Where it may get windy, paper in government department secured by device that grips

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the gripping device

parts.note: a clip grips things

indicators.note: in places the paper inside the department

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A document in a Whitehall office held by a paper clip.
explanation.walkthrough: The FO is the Foreign Office and the FT the Financial Times, both British.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a high exposed top of a sea crag is a breezy spot.

clue.text: Slat by tradition letting some rays through?

indicators.note: letting the rays through means taking them into the middle
through means the rays pass inside the tradition word

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
UV is ultraviolet, a kind of rays

explanation.surface: A blind's slat lets a little sunlight in, as is customary.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one of a set of angled strips in a shutter or vent.

clue.text: Introduction of cog with a square tooth

indicators.note: introduction means just the opening letter

parts.note: nine is a square number, three squared

explanation.surface: Starting a gear with one square tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tooth' sits naturally with cog; it is a mouth tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pointed eye-tooth between the incisors and premolars.

clue.text: Total outsiders accommodated by patient man

indicators.note: accommodated by means housed inside the patient word

parts.note: a case is a patient in medicine

indicators.note: outsiders takes the first and last letters of Total

explanation.surface: Complete strangers are put up by a tolerant fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like an adjective; it is a hospital case. 'man' is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in chess the pieces are called men, and the rook is one.

clue.text: Grounded supporters don't allow scoundrels to follow Colchester United, initially

indicators.note: to follow puts the later pieces after the initials
initially takes the first letter of each of the two club words

parts.note: ban means forbid
heels are cads or scoundrels

explanation.surface: Banned football fans of Colchester United are grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: Colchester United is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: shoe heels are supports that touch the ground, these being a stacked style.

clue.text: See 2
See 9

Lad needing a rise, struggling in paid work

indicators.note: struggling means in difficulty, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A young man needs a raise, struggling in his job.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: receiving a regular fixed wage, so employed.
